_meta.indication: Indicated in adults for the treatment of irritable bowel syndrome with constipation (IBS-C) and chronic idiopathic constipation (CIC).

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial; patients randomized to receive 290 mcg LINZESS or placebo once daily for up to 26 weeks.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients meeting modified Rome II criteria for irritable bowel syndrome with constipation (IBS-C).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: 9/12 week APC 3+1 responder (combined abdominal pain and CSBM responder for at least 9 of the first 12 weeks).
pivotal_trials.n: 804 patients evaluated for efficacy (LINZESS 290 mcg N=401, Placebo N=403) in label Trial 2.
pivotal_trials.result: Combined (APC) responder 12.7% LINZESS vs 3.0% placebo, treatment difference 9.7% [6.1%, 13.4%] (Trial 2); statistically significantly better than placebo.

nct_ctgov.title: Trial of Linaclotide in Patients With Irritable Bowel Syndrome With Constipation (IBS-C)

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial; 290 mcg LINZESS vs placebo once daily for 12 weeks followed by a 4-week randomized withdrawal period.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients meeting modified Rome II criteria for IBS-C.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: 9/12 week APC 3+1 responder (combined abdominal pain and CSBM responder for at least 9 of the first 12 weeks).
pivotal_trials.n: 800 patients evaluated for efficacy (LINZESS 290 mcg N=405, Placebo N=395) in label Trial 1.
pivotal_trials.result: Combined (APC) responder 12.1% LINZESS vs 5.1% placebo, treatment difference 7.0% [3.2%, 10.9%] (Trial 1); replicated the primary endpoint with a modest treatment difference.

nct_ctgov.title: Trial of Linaclotide Administered to Patients With Irritable Bowel Syndrome With Constipation

key_safety: Diarrhea was the most common adverse reaction (20% LINZESS vs 3% placebo in pooled IBS-C trials; 16% vs 5% in CIC trials); severe diarrhea occurred in 2% of LINZESS patients. Other common AEs include abdominal pain, flatulence, and abdominal distension.
target_moa: Guanylate cyclase-C (GC-C) agonist; linaclotide and its active metabolite bind GC-C on the luminal surface of the intestinal epithelium, increasing cGMP and stimulating chloride and bicarbonate secretion.

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: PEDIATRIC RISK — LINZESS is contraindicated in pediatric patients up to 6 years of age; avoid use in patients 6 through 17 years of age. Linaclotide caused deaths in young juvenile mice.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened because the clinical study design was acceptable and the application did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues requiring outside expertise.

summary.text: LINZESS (linaclotide) was submitted August 8, 2011, received August 9, 2011, granted a standard review (not accelerated approval), and approved on the first cycle based on two placebo-controlled Phase 3 IBS-C trials (Trials 1 and 2) and two placebo-controlled CIC trials (Trials 3 and 4); no advisory committee was convened.

citations.quote: The NDA for Linzess was submitted on August 8, 2011, and received on August 9, 2011. The application was granted a standard review. A major amendment received on April 17, 2012 extended the review clock by three months.
The efficacy of LINZESS for the management of symptoms of IBS-C was established in two double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized, multicenter trials in adult patients (Trials 1 and 2).

The data described below reflect exposure to LINZESS in the two double-blind placebo-controlled clinical trials of 1275 adult patients with CIC (Trials 3 and 4). Patients were randomized to receive placebo or 145 mcg LINZESS or 290 mcg LINZESS once daily on an empty stomach, for at least 12 weeks.

This application was not referred to an advisory committee because the clinical study design was acceptable, the application did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues, the application did not raise significant public health questions on the role of the drug in the diagnosis, cure, mitigation, treatment or prevention of disease, and outside expertise was not necessary.
